intervention: DFS recall bound widened 0.1 -> 0.02 (total-NLL 2.30 -> 3.91 nats) and dfs_max_candidates 32 -> 64; everything else v8 verbatim; 150 real predictions in both.
finding: EXACTLY FLAT. Widening the recall bound by 1.6 nats and doubling the candidate cap changed the public score not at all (1.67 -> 1.67). Because v8 and v9 are otherwise byte-identical in configuration and both submitted 150 real predictions, this is a clean single-variable test and the null is informative rather than merely disappointing.

preregistered_read_applied.rule_as_written: recall class converts -> hit rate >> 2.7%; FLAT -> the bound was not binding and the next lever is the DFS TIME budget via the staged kaggle/v10/, NOT more bound widening
preregistered_read_applied.conclusion: The recall bound was NOT the binding constraint. The search was not failing to admit correct candidates for want of probability mass, so giving it more mass and more candidate slots bought nothing. Widening it further is now explicitly ruled out by the preregistration - the next lever is the DFS TIME budget (v10: 60 -> 90 s/task), which is staged in kaggle/v10/.
preregistered_read_applied.what_would_have_falsified_this: Any movement in either direction. A rise would have converted the recall class; a fall would have indicated the wider bound was admitting distractors and costing precision. Neither happened.

caveat_on_resolution: The public leaderboard quantizes at roughly 1/240 = 0.42 points, so 'flat' means the change moved fewer than about one hidden task in either direction. It does not exclude a sub-task-scale effect; it does exclude an effect large enough to matter against the ~10% Sept-1 bar.
